topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture topic and sets expectations regarding complement complexity and nomenclature.

topics.label: Overview, nomenclature, and central C3 activation
topics.groupedBecause: They provide a high-level overview of complement function, clarify naming conventions, and explain the central biochemical activation of C3.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how the alternative, lectin, and classical pathways initiate complement deposition and converge to reach the activation threshold.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the downstream actions of activated complement in driving opsonization, inflammation, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Regulation of complement on host cells
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that protect host tissues from unintended complement attack.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It details how deficiencies in various complement components and regulators manifest in distinct clinical diseases.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement and practical applications
topics.groupedBecause: It explores the strategies pathogens use to evade complement destruction and highlights laboratory and clinical uses of staphylococcal protein A.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the session on complement and previews the next lecture on the adaptive immune system.
